entities.name: Vladivostok
entities.label: Place
entities.summary:
Vladivostok is the largest city and administrative center of Russia's Primorsky Krai, located on the Golden Horn Bay of the Sea of Japan near the borders with China and North Korea. With 600,000 people, it is the dominant city of the Russian Far East and Russia's primary Pacific Ocean port and naval base — a city whose strategic importance has been central to Russian imperial, Soviet, and post-Soviet ambitions in Asia.

The site was a Tungusic Manchu settlement before Russian annexation in 1860 (the Treaty of Beijing), which ceded the Primorye region from the Qing Empire to Russia. The city's name translates as 'Ruler of the East.' The Trans-Siberian Railway terminus (completed 1916) connected Vladivostok to Moscow (9,289 km) and made it the critical link between European Russia and its Pacific possessions. During the Russian Civil War (1918–1922), Vladivostok was occupied by Allied Intervention forces including US, Japanese, British, and Czech troops, serving as the headquarters of the White Army's last stand in Siberia.

Closed to foreigners during most of the Soviet period, Vladivostok's naval base hosted the Pacific Fleet headquarters and nuclear submarines. Mikhail Gorbachev's 1986 Vladivostok Initiative signaled a new Soviet Pacific strategy. Post-Soviet development has focused on making Vladivostok a gateway for Russian trade with Asia — the Eastern Economic Forum meets annually in Vladivostok under Putin, hosting leaders from China, South Korea, Japan, and ASEAN nations.
